description: We are Team Cosmic Eclipse, participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! Our project, "Abandoned But Not Forgotten," focuses on exploring, tracking, and raising awareness about abandoned spacecraft, defunct satellites, space debris, and forgotten space exploration artifacts through an interactive web platform.
summary:
Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is an interactive educational platform that brings the stories of NASA's abandoned and inactive spacecraft to life across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. We developed a digital experience combining a mission archive, interactive hardware maps, 3D inspection, mission timelines, spacecraft comparisons, quizzes, mission detective challenges, and a space exploration game.

The project addresses the challenge of making the history and scientific contributions of abandoned space equipment accessible beyond technical archives and documents. It allows students, educators, and space enthusiasts to discover what these spacecraft were designed to do, what they achieved, why their missions ended, and what remains behind.

This project is important because every abandoned spacecraft represents a milestone in human exploration and scientific discovery. By transforming mission information into interactive storytelling, we aim to inspire curiosity, support space education, and ensure that these remarkable machines are never forgotten.
details: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is an interactive educational platform that brings the stories of NASA's abandoned and inactive spacecraft to life across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. How it works: The platform combines an interactive mission archive, hardware location maps, 3D inspection experiences, mission timelines, spacecraft comparisons, quizzes, Mission Detective challenges, and a space exploration game. Users can discover individual missions, explore their history, understand their scientific achievements, and learn what happened to the equipment after each mission ended. Benefits and intended impact: Spacecraft history is often scattered across technical reports and scientific archives. Our platform transforms this information into an accessible and engaging learning experience for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. We aim to increase curiosity about planetary science, improve awareness of NASA's exploration history, and make scientific information easier to understand through interactive storytelling. Creativity and innovation: We bring together scientific research, interactive maps, 3D experiences, gamification, and storytelling in one educational platform. Rather than simply displaying mission information, we encourage users to actively explore and investigate the legacy of each spacecraft. Technology: The project was developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js/WebGL, with SVG-based fallback experiences. We used web-based development tools and Netlify for deployment. Factors considered: Our team considered scientific accuracy, educational value, accessibility, mobile responsiveness, usability, and performance. We prioritised reliable NASA references and avoided presenting unsupported dates or spacecraft coordinates as established facts. Future development: We aim to expand the archive with additional verified mission records, improve hardware location accuracy, introduce more detailed 3D spacecraft models, and develop further interactive planetary environments and multilingual educational experiences.
